To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The utility values assigned to states of health by individuals in our survey were found to be consistent with the standard gamble method of measurement; (2) the values assigned by individuals in our study were found to be significantly different from those assigned by the general population; and (3) there was no significant difference in the utility values assigned to the states of health by respondents of different ethnic groups.
(1) The utility function of health has a concave shape, and the concavity is greater when the state of health is more severe.

(a) there are no differences in the utility functions of health between the different groups; (b) the utility values of health are not the same as the values of money; and (c) risk aversion is a significant factor affecting the utility function of health.

the utility function of health and the risk aversion of individuals in making health decisions.
